_doc: Per-series Y-axis baselines (floor/ceiling) for chart rendering. Anchored on the 10-year published range so a 0.4pp move in a 2.5-5.5% Fed funds chart visibly traverses ~10% of the panel height instead of vanishing into auto-scale. Style guide §6.1 references this file. visual_qa.py asserts each charted Y-domain matches ±5% of these values.

_rules.floor: Y-axis minimum. May be below the data's actual min so the chart frames historical context.
_rules.ceiling: Y-axis maximum. May be above the data's actual max for the same reason.
_rules.note: Optional rationale for the chosen window.

FEDFUNDS.label: Federal Funds Rate
FEDFUNDS.note: Covers ZIRP through 5.5% peak; gives recent +/-0.5pp moves visible amplitude

DGS2.label: 2-Year Treasury Yield
DGS2.note: Mirrors DGS10 range; 2Y sits below 10Y in normal regimes

DGS30.label: 30-Year Treasury Yield
DGS30.note: Long bond range; less volatile than DGS2/DGS10

UNRATE.label: Unemployment Rate
UNRATE.note: Excludes COVID 14.8% spike (would crush all other variation)

CPILFESL_YOY.label: Core CPI YoY
CPILFESL_YOY.note: Less volatile than headline; tighter window OK

PCEPILFE_YOY.label: Core PCE YoY
PCEPILFE_YOY.note: The Fed's preferred gauge; primary target window

GDPC1_YOY.label: Real GDP YoY
GDPC1_YOY.note: Excludes COVID -9% trough; recession-band visible above floor

UMCSENT.label: UMich Consumer Sentiment
UMCSENT.note: Index level; 50 floor avoids dramatic-looking moves at the bottom
